blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. The reports count condos and townhomes together in one line, so this table cannot separate the two. Shares are this community’s count divided by the Coquitlam total for condos and townhomes that month.

blocks.text: Condo buildings in Coquitlam East
Bromley Manor — 450 Bromley Street

A wood-frame low-rise apartment building across from Mundy Park, listed under the board sub-area Coquitlam East. Current listings record freehold strata title, underground parking, a caretaker and shared laundry / in-suite laundry by unit, and one listing describes the building as pet-welcoming; a current listing also describes a proactive strata with a large contingency fund. Year built is not settled in public sources: most current listings record 1991, one records 1990 — 1991 is used here and the conflict is noted.
455 Bromley Street
A second apartment address directly by Bromley Manor. A 2019 brokerage feature sheet for a unit records an apartment built in 1991 and carries the line "Pet/Rental: Not allowed".
Streets, schools and getting around Coquitlam East

items.t: Where the condo stock concentrates: it barely concentrates at all. The sub-area is detached-house streets under the City's small-scale residential zones; the one apartment building sits at the southern edge on Bromley Street, across from Mundy Park by the Austin Avenue shops, and the townhome complexes sit on the Lansdowne Drive / Eagleridge Drive slopes.
SnapStats publishes medians at community level only: the Coquitlam condos & townhomes median was $625,000 in September 2026 ($687/sqft, 96% sale-to-list, 23 days on market).
Main roads: David Avenue, Coast Meridian Road, Lansdowne Drive, Lougheed Highway and Austin Avenue.

Transit anchor: Coquitlam Central Station (Millennium Line Evergreen Extension and West Coast Express), at Lougheed Highway and Pinetree Way, is the main station for east Coquitlam and sits west of the sub-area.

blocks.text: Good to know about Coquitlam East

items.t: Bromley Manor's build year is not settled in public sources. Most current listings say 1991; one says 1990.

The sub-area's name collision is industrial, not residential. The only new "Eagle Ridge" strata product on this side of the city is an industrial park on Barnet Highway — a buyer searching "Eagle Ridge strata" will surface warehouse units alongside the 1980s villas on Eagleridge Drive.

Eagle Ridge Court (1170 Lansdowne Drive) sits on the lower slope in this sub-area's frame, while Greyhawke Estates (1495 Lansdowne Drive) is placed by the building directory in Westwood Plateau — same street, different board geography, different price conversation.
One strata sale a month is the whole attached story.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Coquitlam East

items.t: Form B diligence (both counted strata complexes): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. Listing-level rental/pet lines here are listing data, not bylaws — the Form B and registered bylaws govern. Both counted complexes are 1980s wood-frame strata, so the depreciation report, CRF balance and any envelope/roof history in the Form B package are the core diligence items.
Fee-simple homes (the sub-area's detached stock): No fee-simple townhouse complex is counted in, so this is the rule for the detached houses a Coquitlam East townhouse buyer cross-shops.

Coquitlam zoning and SSMUH: small-scale residential zones R-1, R-2 and R-3 under Zoning Bylaw No. 3000, 1996 — minimum lot size for subdivision is 650 m² with 18.5 m width for R-1 and R-3, and 465 m² with 12.5 m width for R-2. Coquitlam's adopted SSMUH rules allow up to 3 units on lots 280 m² or smaller and up to 4 units on lots larger than 280 m² and under 4,050 m², including secondary suites and carriage or laneway homes; lots not connected to municipal water or sewer are outside the SSMUH rules. The Interim OCP Bylaws 5511/5512, adopted April 27, 2026, supersede OCP No. 3479 as the plan frame.

Watercourse and hazards: the Watercourse Protection Development Permit Area covers all areas within 50 metres of the top of bank of any watercourse in Northeast Coquitlam and within 30 metres in the rest of Coquitlam; Zoning Bylaw s. 519 sets flood protection setbacks from watercourses and s. 523 covers riparian areas — a live check on the ravine- and forest-edge lots around the Atlin Place pocket.

blocks.text: Good to know about Coquitlam East

items.t: One street, three sub-areas.
Eagle Ridge Court started as rentals.

The Atlin Place pocket backs onto protected forest. Cedar Green listings describe the complex on the edge of Riverview Forest with a patio backing onto the greenbelt, and The Terraces sits in the same Riverview Heights pocket — the forest edge, plus Mundy Park's trails nearby, is the pocket's amenity, not a strata facility.
A strata sale a month is the whole attached story.

The "Eagle Ridge" project on Barnet Highway is not housing. IntraUrban Eagle Ridge (2660 Barnet Highway) is strata industrial/showroom product zoned IL-1 — it surfaces in "Eagle Ridge" searches and is neither a condo nor a townhome.

Coquitlam's plan frame changed in 2026. The Interim OCP Bylaws 5511/5512, adopted April 27, 2026, supersede OCP No. 3479 — any east-side document still citing OCP No. 3479 as the current plan is out of date; Zoning Bylaw No. 3000, 1996 remains the zoning bylaw.

blocks.text: Coquitlam East home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

10 townhomes sold in Coquitlam East with a median price of $802,250 (the middle half sold between $774,750 and $953,750), taking a median of 12 days to sell at 98.3% of the last list price; 20% sold above list. They had a median $602 per square foot, a median year built of 1998 and a median strata fee of $413 a month. 5 condos sold in Coquitlam East with a median price of $515,000, taking a median of 16 days to sell at 96.6% of the last list price; 20% sold above list. They had a median $511 per square foot, a median year built of 1990 and a median strata fee of $552 a month.
